This is the authoritative record; NOTICE and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md are views of it and must agree.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: it is not proof that everything borrowed is declared. Nothing in this
repository can prove that. A file copied from a project we do not vendor, with its upstream
attribution removed, is invisible to every automated check we have. See the residual-risk section of
THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, which lists the known gaps in full.
Scope: files that live in this tree. Donor code COMPILED IN PLACE from the external/TabularEditor
submodule has no path here (it is not our file); it is described in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md prose.

the Borrowing code section at the top of THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md.

entries.author: Tabular Editor ApS
entries.evidence: Read external/TabularEditor/LICENSE at the pinned submodule commit: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2025 Tabular Editor ApS. Copied rather than compiled in place so the rename fixup can be repaired without editing the pristine submodule. Upstream master carries the same code. The only local changes are the attribution header, a keyword filter (IsNeverATable) on the one condition that reads a keyword as a table, one return changed to continue, the KPIs added to the full dependency-tree rebuild, a row-scan scope tracker so a bare [column] binds to the scanned table (innermost scan first, unique names in an unknown scan), and the rewrite of a KPI's generated helper names, and a row scan over FILTER, ALL, CALCULATETABLE, TOPN, SAMPLE or TOPNSKIP of one plain table name reading that table's row, one table (RowScanSpecs) of which arguments of each row-scan function are read in the scanned row and which in the caller's context, and the KPI helper rewrite acting only at the occurrences bound to the helper, SUMMARIZE reading a bare name as a column only where a groupBy argument names it, a scan of CURRENTGROUP () inside GROUPBY reading that GROUPBY's table, and a scan of a VAR reading the one table the VAR's expression stands for (6 Oct, solfx: Sol A6 findings 3 and 4, then fix round 2; 5 Oct, join 11: read the LICENSE again at the same pin, still MIT, Copyright (c) 2025 Tabular Editor ApS).
entries.notes: Copied rather than compiled in place because the donor reads RETURN, NOT, IN, VAR, ASC, DESC, AND and OR before a bracket as a table, then stops the walk of the whole formula at the first table it cannot find, so a rename left every reference after them on the old name; it also never visits a measure's KPI, so a rename left KPI expressions on the old name. Semanticus.Core no longer compiles the donor file and compiles this copy.
entries.upstreamEquivalence: modified-subset: a keyword that is never a table (RETURN, NOT, IN, VAR, ASC, DESC, AND, OR) is not read as the table of a following bracket, and a reference to a table the model lacks skips that one reference (continue) instead of ending the walk (return), and each measure's KPI joins the full dependency-tree rebuild so a rename rewrites its status, target and trend, and a bare [column] inside a row-scan function (SUMX, FILTER, ADDCOLUMNS and the like) is read from the table that function scans (open scans are searched from the innermost out, then the home table; TOPN, SAMPLE and TOPNSKIP name their table as argument 2 or 3; RANKX scans only its expression, and every function reads only its documented per-row arguments in the scanned row, the others in the caller's context, one table RowScanSpecs, CALCULATETABLE opening no scope, SUMMARIZE reading a bare name as a column only when a groupBy argument names it, a scan of CURRENTGROUP () inside GROUPBY reading that GROUPBY's table, and a scan of a VAR reading the one table its expression stands for, a VAR name visible only inside its own VAR ... RETURN block, which ends when the expression it stands in ends and gives back what it hid, and that is visible only in the expressions after its own declaration, never inside its own initializer (join 12, the j12fx round, then join 13); a scan of a table the walk cannot know binds only a column name that is unique in the model and the home table's), and the generated KPI helpers [_<name> Goal], [_<name> Status] and [_<name> Trend] are rewritten when the base measure is renamed, at the occurrences the walk bound to the helper only, and a row scan whose table argument is FILTER, ALL, CALCULATETABLE, TOPN, SAMPLE or TOPNSKIP over one plain table name reads the row of that table. Every other line is byte-identical to the donor.

entries.doNotUpgradeWithout: Re-reading the LICENSE file at the NEW pinned commit and re-hashing the upstream body. Do not move the version pin forward because a newer corpus has more rules: the pin is the point at which the licence was actually read, and bodySha256 here is the hash of OUR file, which is a modified subset, so it cannot detect an upstream relicence on its own. This entry is MIT on evidence, not on plausibility, which is what the previous TabularEditor/BestPracticeRules entry got wrong: that upstream published no licence at all (LICENSE and LICENSE.md both HTTP 404, GitHub API license: null) and was correctly recorded UNVERIFIED until it was replaced. Do not reintroduce that corpus.
entries.upstreamEquivalence: modified-subset: 69 of the 71 upstream rules, 2 of those scope-narrowed, plus 5 Semanticus-authored SEM_ rules; documentation links stripped from 29 fields; PERCENTAGE_FORMATTING FixExpression literals normalized from the six-character \u003B sequence to real semicolons; DATA_COLUMNS_MUST_HAVE_A_SOURCE_COLUMN gained a calculation-group guard in 974f28f6 because calculation-group columns are typed as data columns but are not loaded from a query (D-009). Four rules gained a Semanticus-only ExemptFieldParameters flag, FORMAT_FLAG_COLUMNS_AS_YES/NO_VALUE_STRINGS accepts the three-part Yes/No format string from every flag type it catches rather than from an Int64 one only, and DATECOLUMN_FORMATSTRING and MONTHCOLUMN_FORMATSTRING both flag only a column with no format string at all, writing ISO yyyy-mm-dd and MMMM yyyy respectively (27 Sep). The two measure-scoped format rules, INTEGER_FORMATTING and PERCENTAGE_FORMATTING, flag only a measure with no format string expression whose format string is made only of plain number characters (0 # , . ; ( ) space - %, plus quoted punctuation such as "-") with at least one 0 or # placeholder (PERCENTAGE_FORMATTING also needing a %, INTEGER_FORMATTING needing none), and INTEGER_FORMATTING also flags a measure with no format at all, so neither can write over a date, time, currency, unit, word or dynamic format; each gained a Description it did not have upstream (28 Sep, rounds 5 and 7). In round 8 (28 Sep) both moved to severity 1 (advice) and neither fix is offered on a format string that is already there, because no fix writes over one: INTEGER_FORMATTING's fix only fills a blank format string, and PERCENTAGE_FORMATTING's never applies, since that rule only raises a format that has a %. In round 9 (28 Sep, THE FORMAT FILL RULE) INTEGER_FORMATTING's Description promises its fill only where Semanticus proves a whole number, and DATECOLUMN_FORMATSTRING's and MONTHCOLUMN_FORMATSTRING's Descriptions call them advice with no one-click fix. FORMAT_FLAG_COLUMNS_AS_YES/NO_VALUE_STRINGS never raises a DateTime column for its name (28 Sep, round 7). REDUCE_USAGE_OF_CALCULATED_TABLES spares a calculated table whose whole expression is CALENDAR or CALENDARAUTO, or ADDCOLUMNS over one; UNNECESSARY_COLUMNS never raises its table's IsKey column or a column with the Semanticus_SourceKey annotation (every part of a key a model spec declares, because TOM holds IsKey on one column per table); and INTEGER_FORMATTING adds #,##0 and #,##0.0 to the formats it treats as already styled, beside #,0 and #,0.0 (28 Sep, the Plan statement check). Every difference is enumerated in Semanticus.Analysis/Rules/BPARules-PowerBI.PROVENANCE.md, ISAVAILABLEINMDX_FALSE_NONATTRIBUTE_COLUMNS gained a plain-words Description saying what the fix does for Excel and for Power BI reports (12 Oct, wording only: expression, severity and fix unchanged; the licence was not re-read for this wording change and the version pin did not move). So bodySha256 pins OUR file and the upstream pin is verified by refetching the commit.

entries.upstream: the webview production dependency closure, bundled at build time
entries.author: multiple; see dependencyClosure and the notices section
entries.evidence: Every package name, version and licence below is read from Semanticus.VSCode/webview/package-lock.json (non-dev entries). The gate compares that lockfile to this list in BOTH directions, so a new production dependency cannot enter the lockfile or the bundle without failing until it is declared here and in the notices. Licence holders for the non-MIT families were read from the installed packages: zrender BSD-3-Clause (Copyright (c) 2017, Baidu Inc.), d3-ease BSD-3-Clause (Copyright 2010-2021 Mike Bostock; Copyright 2001 Robert Penner), react MIT (Copyright (c) Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates), tslib 0BSD (Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation), echarts Apache-2.0.
entries.headerWaiverReason: Generated build output. It carries esbuild/rollup extracted legal comments inline; the authoritative record is dependencyClosure below plus the lockfile.
entries.scopeLimit: This declares the production dependency CLOSURE the bundle is built from, taken from the lockfile. It does NOT prove which of those packages survived tree-shaking into the emitted file, and 8 of them are @types packages that emit no runtime code at all. Proving per-package presence in the emitted bundle is not attempted and is not claimed.

entries.upstreamPath: OFL.txt (licence); the binary is the Latin subset of the variable font
entries.author: The Instrument Sans Project Authors
entries.evidence: Read OFL.txt at commit 7fa22308a3d0c94ee2b3cd537a1196b65db34a3e of Instrument/instrument-sans (raw.githubusercontent.com, 8 Oct 2026): SIL Open Font License 1.1, Copyright 2022 The Instrument Sans Project Authors, no Reserved Font Name declared. It is identical (line endings aside) to the InstrumentSans-OFL.txt that ships beside the font. The OFL allows use, embedding, subsetting and redistribution of the font with that notice and licence text. The woff2 is the Latin-subset variable file the Semanticus site build self-hosts; it was NOT compared byte for byte with an upstream release file, so bodySha256 pins our copy, not the upstream bytes.
